chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni said:
The divorce of the mute woman is that he takes her head-covering and places it on her head, then he separates from her.
ai.seo_question: How is a divorce legally executed for a mute woman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a specific legal mechanism for divorcing a mute woman (al-akhraṣ) who lacks the verbal capacity to consent, relying instead on the symbolic act of the husband placing her head-covering (miqna'ah) on her head as a sign of separation. This procedure highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on adapting ritual actions to the physical realities of the parties involved, ensuring the validity of the divorce through clear, observable gestures rather than spoken words. It underscores the principle that in the absence of speech, physical indicators serve as the primary medium for conveying legal intent.
